title: 235. Stone Game II

examples.explanation: If Alice takes one pile at the beginning, Bob takes two piles, then Alice takes 2 piles again. Alice can get 2 + 4 + 4 = 10 piles in total. If Alice takes two piles at the beginning, then Bob can take three piles, and Alice can get 2 + 7 = 9 piles in total. If Alice takes three piles at the beginning, then Bob takes all the four remaining piles, and Alice can get 9 piles in total. So the maximum Alice can get is 10.

hints: Use dynamic programming: the states are (i, m) for the answer of piles[i:] given m.

If 2*m >= n - i the current player can take all remaining piles. Otherwise try every X in 1..2*m and let the opponent start at i + X with M = max(m, X), keeping the take that maximizes suffix[i] - opponent's score.
